Subject: Private VPC topology inventory & control/data-plane gap check

Hi Markus —

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing our handoff package for the FinBank private deployment and need a short validation from Redwood on a couple of control/data-plane topics before we lock the cutover window. Attached are two baseline files: finbank_vpc_inventory_v1.xlsx and finbank_network_diagram_v1.pdf.

Topline asks:
- Can you confirm the recommended control-plane ingress model (private link vs. customer-provided proxy) and the expected ports/fqdns?
- We need explicit guidance on where mTLS termination is expected (customer edge vs. Redwood sidecar) and whether Redwood supports client cert rotation tied to our HSM KMS.
- Clarify egress expectations for logging/metrics: do agents push to a customer collector or to Redwood-managed collectors across the peering?
- Any considerations for cross-AZ MTU and jumbo frame requirements (we run an SD-WAN overlay in some locations).

We are hoping to have feedback by EOD Tuesday (48 hours) so we can finalize the change window. If useful, let's do a 40-minute working session — propose Wed 9:00–10:00 PT.

Attachments: finbank_vpc_inventory_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), finbank_network_diagram_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kim Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-25T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC topology inventory & control/data-plane gap check

Sanjay —

Appreciate the packet. Quick read-through and a short plan below; I'll schedule the Wed 9:00 PT slot unless you prefer otherwise. I've attached our reference diagram (redwood_private_vpc_reference_diagram_v2.pdf) so you can map FinBank items to our recommendation.

High-level answers and actions: 
- Control-plane ingress model: recommended pattern is a customer-controlled private link or VPN endpoint that terminates at a dedicated control-plane gateway (no public ingress). We support an optional customer-side proxy (TLS passthrough) when customers require an outbound-only model for compliance. Expect ports 443 (API/TLS) and 8443 (internal control-channel) across the peering.

- mTLS and cert rotation: Redwood expects mTLS between sidecar and control-plane with mutual auth. Customer edge may terminate north-south in the proxy if you need central inspection; recommend we keep pod-to-control mTLS intact. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for signing keys and support automated rotation windows; rotation can be scheduled and rolled back by policy in our control plane.

- Egress for telemetry: two supported patterns — (1) Push agents to customer collectors over the private peering (preferred when you want SIEM ownership), or (2) Redwood-managed collectors that forward aggregated telemetry to your SIEM via a secure tunnel. We'll document bandwidth expectations for both.

- MTU considerations: we generally advise a 1500 baseline; if your SD-WAN uses jumbo frames, we recommend testing end-to-end with a staging pod before cutover. Issues usually show up in KV-cache replication and large model shard transfers.

Planned next steps (proposed during the Wed session):
1) Map inventory rows to our reference diagram and mark control-plane endpoints.
2) Validate egress route you want for logs and metrics and confirm BGP/NAT behavior.
3) Walk through cert rotation windows and KMS handshake steps.
4) Identify DR failover path (secondary region) and confirm replication RPO expectations.

I've put Neha on the thread for the DR/ops-runbook items and Kim for network specifics.

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_reference_diagram_v2.pdf

--
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private VPC topology inventory & control/data-plane gap check

Sanjay / Markus —

Thanks — reviewed the diagram and inventory quickly. A few specific gap items we should cover in the session (I'll paste as bullets so ops can verify against the spreadsheet):

- Control-plane telemetry path: the diagram shows control-plane telemetry routed through the customer inspection proxy. If that proxy performs TLS termination, we need to confirm that it will re-establish mTLS to Redwood or that the proxy will inject a trusted client cert. Otherwise control-plane observability will be broken.

- KV-cache and model shard replication: large model transfers (checkpoint / shard sync) can trigger MTU issues on overlays. Recommend: pin model state to a dedicated pool for initial syncs, then allow dynamic sharding. We'll add an explicit pre-cutover test for a 4GB model sync.

- Egress firewall rules: please verify that outbound rules allow TCP 443 to our aggregator endpoints and that your NAT gateway has a consistent SNAT range we can map to for allowlisting.

- DR path: include a minimal secondary-region sketch. If we rely on cross-region replication, we need to agree on encryption-in-flight and cold-start timing (we have a 30–45m warmup for large models).

I've attached a small CSV (controlplane-egress-matrix.csv) that maps our recommended ports and protocols to your inventory sheet columns — please drop it into the workbook or I can join and edit live during the call.

Kim
Network & Deploy Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
